topics.title: Univariate data
points: Categorical data: nominal (no order) or ordinal (ordered). Numerical data: discrete (counted) or continuous (measured).
Centre: mean \(\bar{x} = \dfrac{\sum x}{n}\) (affected by outliers) and median (resistant). Spread: range, \(\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1\), standard deviation \(s\).
Outliers lie below \(Q_1 - 1.5 \times \text{IQR}\) or above \(Q_3 + 1.5 \times \text{IQR}\).
Shape: symmetric, positively skewed (tail to the right), negatively skewed (tail to the left).
Displays: bar charts for categorical data; histograms, dot plots, stem plots and boxplots for numerical data.

topics.title: Investigating relationships
points: Explanatory variable on the \(x\)-axis, response variable on the \(y\)-axis.
Describe a scatterplot by direction (positive or negative), form (linear or non-linear) and strength (weak, moderate, strong).
Pearson’s correlation coefficient: \(-1 \le r \le 1\). It only measures linear relationships.
Correlation does not mean causation: a third variable may explain both.
Two-way tables and segmented bar charts compare two categorical variables.

topics.title: Percentages, interest and recursion
points: Percentage change \(= \dfrac{\text{change}}{\text{original}} \times 100\%\). GST: price \(\times 1.1\); GST in a total \(= \dfrac{\text{total}}{11}\).
Simple interest: \(I = \dfrac{PrT}{100}\); total value \(A = P + I\).
Compound interest: \(A = P\left(1 + \dfrac{r}{100}\right)^n\).
Linear recurrence \(u_{n+1} = u_n + d\) (simple interest, flat-rate depreciation). Geometric recurrence \(u_{n+1} = Ru_n\) (compound growth or decay).
Inflation reduces purchasing power; compare costs in today’s dollars.
topics.explain: Explain why compound interest grows faster than simple interest over time.

topics.title: Matrices
points: Order = rows \(\times\) columns. Add or subtract matrices only of the same order.
\(AB\) exists if the number of columns of \(A\) equals the number of rows of \(B\): \((m \times n)(n \times p)\) gives an \(m \times p\) matrix.
Matrix multiplication is not usually commutative: \(AB \neq BA\).

For \(A = \begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix}\): \(\det A = ad - bc\) and \(A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{ad - bc}\begin{bmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{bmatrix}\), which exists only if \(\det A \neq 0\).
Matrices store data in tables and can solve simultaneous equations.

topics.title: Graphs and networks
points: A graph has vertices joined by edges; the degree of a vertex is the number of edges at it.
Euler trail (every edge once): exists if exactly 0 or 2 vertices have odd degree. Euler circuit (returns to start): every degree is even.
Hamiltonian path: visits every vertex once. Hamiltonian cycle: also returns to the start.
Connected planar graphs satisfy Euler’s formula \(v - e + f = 2\).
Trees, spanning trees and shortest paths solve real problems such as routes and cabling.

topics.title: Linear relations and measurement
points: Linear model: \(y = a + bx\), where \(a\) is the intercept and \(b\) the gradient (rate of change).
Simultaneous equations: solve by substitution, elimination or graphing. Break-even is where cost \(=\) revenue.
Pythagoras: \(c^2 = a^2 + b^2\). Right triangles: \(\sin\theta = \dfrac{O}{H}\), \(\cos\theta = \dfrac{A}{H}\), \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{O}{A}\).
Sine rule \(\dfrac{a}{\sin A} = \dfrac{b}{\sin B}\); cosine rule \(c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab\cos C\).
Similar figures with scale factor \(k\): lengths \(\times k\), areas \(\times k^2\), volumes \(\times k^3\).
Circle \(A = \pi r^2\); cylinder \(V = \pi r^2 h\); sphere \(V = \tfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3\).
